abstract: Maintains network hydraulic capacity and delivery water temperature records
system_message:
You are the District heating engineering lead (ENG), responsible for maintaining network hydraulic capacity and delivery water temperature records as well as pipeline corrosion monitoring across municipal heating plans.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Pipeline corrosion monitoring（CORR）
information_points.content:
ENG-CORR-OZA：According to acoustic ultrasonic pipe inspection logs for the Deep geothermal absorption pump network, the annual inner pipe wall degradation rate across the primary distribution network loop is 0.08 mm/a.
ENG-CORR-K5F：According to acoustic ultrasonic pipe inspection logs for the Industrial waste-heat recovery loop, the annual inner pipe wall degradation rate across the primary distribution network loop is 0.12 mm/a.
ENG-CORR-CMN：According to acoustic ultrasonic pipe inspection logs for the Centralized biomass cogeneration scheme, the annual inner pipe wall degradation rate across the primary distribution network loop is 0.16 mm/a.

information_points.title: Maintains network hydraulic capacity and delivery water temperature records（HYDR）
information_points.content:
ENG-HYDR-5WZ：For the Deep geothermal absorption pump network in France, hydraulic peak capacity is not certified for the winter peak load scenario, and the minimum delivery water temperature is 80 degC at the contracted delivery sub-station boundary during freezing conditions.
ENG-HYDR-04Q：For the Deep geothermal absorption pump network in Germany, hydraulic peak capacity is certified based on formal verification that distribution pressure loss remains within safe operational limits during a winter peak load scenario, and the minimum delivery water temperature is 95 degC at the contracted delivery sub-station boundary during freezing conditions.
ENG-HYDR-G8E：For the Centralized biomass cogeneration scheme in Germany, hydraulic peak capacity is certified for the winter peak load scenario, and the minimum delivery water temperature reaches 95 degC at the contracted delivery sub-station boundary during freezing conditions.
ENG-HYDR-HJG：For the Industrial waste-heat recovery loop in Germany, hydraulic peak capacity is not certified under the winter peak load scenario, while the minimum delivery water temperature is 90 degC at the contracted delivery sub-station boundary during freezing conditions.
